blindSummary:
This state/province's equality law of 1984 protects the attribute of "gender history," defined as a person who "identifies as a member of the opposite sex by living, or seeking to live, as a member of the opposite sex." This is a narrower, medically-inflected, binary formulation than the "gender identity" language used in a neighbouring state/province and in the federal sex-discrimination law. A non-binary or gender-nonconforming visitor may not meet the state-law definition and would rely solely on federal coverage for a state-level complaint. This state/province has no anti-vilification offence (civil or criminal) and no statutory charter of rights binding public authorities.

Reform is underway: a 2024 registration amendment received assent on 26 September 2024, removing medical and surgical prerequisites for registration of a sex or gender change, with substantive commencement by proclamation. This feeds back into the scope of "gender history" for complaints purposes but is not yet fully in force.

The narrower protective vocabulary and the absence of both a vilification offence and a rights charter leave fewer state-level remedies than elsewhere in the country, even though the federal floor is unchanged. A neighbouring state/province has a human-rights act binding public authorities and a conversion-practice prohibition in force since 2020; this state/province lacks both structural review and the specific coercion safeguard.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: the consolidated text of this state/province's 1984 equality law was not retrievable at fetch time (the state legislation portal blocks automated fetches); the companion official explainer below quotes the operative definitions - the law protects the attribute 'gender history', defined by living, or seeking to live, as a member of the opposite sex, with complaint eligibility tied to recognition certificates or registry change under the civil registration framework.

The state government's public information page on gender-history discrimination: unlawful to discriminate because of gender history under this state/province's 1984 equality law; a person has a gender history only if they 'identify as a member of the opposite sex by living, or seeking to live, as a member of the opposite sex'; 'gender reassigned person' is defined through a 2000 gender-reassignment recognition certificate or a civil-registration change - a binary, certificate/medical-anchored formulation; complaint route is the state equality commissioner, 12-month filing limit, exceptions list.

The state government's media statement (16 April 2024): reforms to remove barriers for the LGBTQIA+ community - trans and gender-diverse residents will no longer be required to undergo medical or surgical reassignment to register a change of sex or gender, via a streamlined administrative process in the civil registration, implementing law-reform recommendations (the reform received assent 26 September 2024).

A community legal centre's fact sheet for trans and gender-diverse young people in this state/province and their families: explains the choice between state (the 'gender history' route) and federal (the national sex-discrimination law's gender-identity/cisgender attributes) complaints - a complainant can use one track, not both - evidencing how this state/province's narrower definitions push claimants onto federal coverage.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2024 registration amendment (assent 26 September 2024, substantive commencement still by proclamation) is a resident registration reform; until it is in force the state complaint definition still runs through certificates and registry changes rather than self-declared identity.
